title: Session diagnostics and implicit-refresh ergonomics across Py/TS/Go SDKs
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: Adds session-level diagnostics, implicit credential refresh helpers, and small ergonomic tweaks to stream iterables across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Bumps Python to 2.5.0, TypeScript to 1.27.0, Go SDK helpers to v1.8.0. No customer-facing API breaking changes expected.
body: Context: Customers running long-lived streaming sessions frequently hit opaque auth errors mid-stream and lack actionable telemetry to triage reauth races. This PR introduces a small, cross-SDK surface to improve diagnostics and a compact implicit-refresh helper that reduces boilerplate without changing contract semantics. Goals: 1) surface session-level diagnostic tags and a lightweight progress heartbeat for stream consumers, 2) provide an opt-in implicitRefresh() helper that schedules token refresh and coordinates in-flight requests to avoid 'double-refresh' races, 3) align ergonomics across Python/TS/Go and bump packaged helper versions. What changed: added SessionDiagnostics and implicitRefresh helpers in each SDK package; added a streaming-heartbeat event to the internal wire (non-breaking, opt-in); normalized retry presets to explicitly include an auth-retry predicate and jittered backoff defaults; example snippets and migration notes updated in each SDK README. Checklist: - [x] Implement Python implicitRefresh + diagnostics (redwood-sdk-python) - [x] Implement TS implicitRefresh + diagnostics (redwood-sdk-typescript) - [x] Implement Go connector shim with diagnostics (redwood-sdk-go) - [x] Add unit + integration tests for cross-language behavior - [x] Update quickstarts and release notes Rationale: Many support tickets (ENG-2145) showed similar patterns where SDK consumers duplicated token refresh logic with subtle race conditions. This PR centralizes a pragmatic pattern while keeping explicit control available for advanced users. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in and existing usages remain unchanged unless teams enable the helper via the client options. Migration notes: to enable implicit refresh, set client.options.implicitRefresh=true (Python: Client(options={implicit_refresh: True}), TS: new Client({implicitRefresh: true}), Go: ClientWithOptions(Opts{ImplicitRefresh:true}). Tests: local unit tests for auth handoff, simulated long-running streams asserting single refresh per expiry event, and e2e smoke against staging token service. Related: ENG-2145, ENG-2199, linked demo in linear https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2145/stream-auth-races. Security review: minimal — no new network calls except token endpoint already used by SDKs; refresh coordination only touches local in-memory token cache. Telemetry: session diagnostic tags are emitted as structured fields on existing span: session.id, session.latency_ms, session.auth_refresh_count. Version bumps: python v2.5.0, typescript v1.27.0, go helper v1.8.0. Notes for maintainers: watch for increased telemetry volume in high-throughput customers; default sample rate remains unchanged.
commits: 3 commits: 1) core: session diagnostics + heartbeat proto and tests; 2) sdk-python: implicitRefresh helper, README examples, version bump to 2.5.0; 3) sdk-ts/go: mirror helpers and tests, sync examples and bump versions
